assessment.nobel_worthiness: The heterogeneous-firm framework changed how trade economists think about who gains from trade, why only some firms export, and how reallocation across firms drives aggregate gains. It built a new empirical and theoretical agenda that extends the earlier new-trade-theory recognition. It has been applied widely in trade, macro and labour, and in policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central model. Helpman's firm-level work, including Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple and Helpman-Itskhoki-Redding on labour-market frictions, is the main complementary contribution. Redding is influential, especially in quantitative spatial work, but his contribution is more derivative or adjacent to the core, so I leave him out of the core pair.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of confirmation across many countries and datasets. The framework is textbook material and the timing is mature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views Redding as co-core
Whether Helpman is better paired with Grossman (B031) for his political-economy work
Some later empirical work questions the quantitative size of the selection gains

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Random-coefficients demand estimation with endogenous prices (BLP), together with dynamic industry models, made structural industrial organisation empirically operational. It is now standard in merger review, antitrust, trade, health and environmental economics, and it has real policy impact.
assessment.attribution: The BLP estimator (Berry, Levinsohn, Pakes 1995) is clearly attributable. Pakes also carries the dynamic-game and Ericson-Pakes work, and Berry carries the inversion argument. Bresnahan and Reiss are important contributors from the earlier NEIO tradition, and some credit would be left out of a three-person prize.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of use and refinement make this a mature contribution with extensive validation.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer to credit the NEIO pioneers Bresnahan and Reiss
Persistent methodological debate about the sensitivity of structural IO results to functional-form assumptions
Limit of three laureates

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work shows how technology and trade reshape labour demand, polarise job markets and affect local labour markets. It combines convincing identification with a clear economic framework and has had major influence on public debate and policy. It blends data discovery with an explanatory framework, which I value.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to both the task-based and trade-shock strands. Hanson is key to the China-shock design, with Dorn as a co-author. Katz's earlier skill-demand work is foundational but overlaps with other candidates. The task-approach contributions of Acemoglu and Restrepo, and Levy and Murnane, are outside this ballot entry.
assessment.maturity: The China-shock papers date from 2013 onward and are heavily cited, with ongoing re-examination. The work is mature, though still debated on magnitudes and persistence.
uncertainties: Attribution across a diffuse group, including the earlier task literature
Ongoing debate about the persistence and size of the trade-shock effects
Possible overlap with the recent 2024 and 2025 prizes in technology and growth

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The law-and-finance programme shifted attention to legal institutions as determinants of financial development and corporate governance. It opened a large empirical agenda in finance, law and development, and it links closely to the institutions theme in recent prizes.
assessment.attribution: La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer and Vishny are the core authors of the original papers. A three-name prize would have to leave out Vishny, which is a real attribution problem. Shleifer's broader contributions add weight.
assessment.maturity: Work from the late 1990s has been tested for a long time, which supports maturity. The evidence for causal claims has weakened.
uncertainties: Replication and measurement critiques of the legal-origins and anti-director indices
Whether causal inference about legal origin holds up
Exclusion of Vishny from a three-person prize

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The sufficient-statistics approach and the empirical taxable-income work bridge theory and evidence in public finance. They reshaped how tax policy is evaluated and are very influential in both research and policy design.
assessment.attribution: Saez is central to the elasticity-of-taxable-income and optimal-tax synthesis. Chetty is central to the sufficient-statistics methodology. Slemrod and Stantcheva have strong contributions, but they are more peripheral to the core. Saez also appears on B026 and Chetty on B012, so their credit could be split across entries.
assessment.maturity: Mature in public economics and widely adopted. Chetty's more recent work is newer.
uncertainties: Overlap of laureate credit across B012, B021 and B026
Whether the committee prefers a more theory-centred optimal-tax prize (for example Mirrlees-Diamond lineage)
Age and timing of the younger contributors

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework underlies modern monetary policy analysis and central-bank practice, and rule-based policy evaluation has had large practical influence. It is among the most consequential macro frameworks that remain unrecognised.
assessment.attribution: Credit is very diffuse across Taylor, Woodford, Gali, Calvo, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets, Gertler and others. Any group of three leaves out several clearly important contributors. This is the main weakness.
assessment.maturity: The framework is well established, with decades of application, though the post-2008 and post-2021 inflation experiences have prompted reappraisal.
uncertainties: Severe attribution diffuseness
The 2021-23 inflation experience challenged parts of the framework
Overlap with earlier macro prizes for rational expectations and policy

assessment.nobel_worthiness: GMM estimators for dynamic panel data are everyday tools in applied microeconomics, growth and corporate finance, and the work gave the field a practical standard for estimating dynamic relationships with unobserved heterogeneity. The contribution is methodologically important, though narrower in conceptual scope than the leading candidates.
assessment.attribution: Arellano-Bond (1991) and Arellano-Bover and Blundell-Bond (1995, 1998) are well-defined. Anderson-Hsiao and Holtz-Eakin, Newey and Rosen are earlier contributions that complicate the credit. Blundell's wider work on labour supply and consumption could also count.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with decades of use. The proliferation-of-instruments problem is known and documented.
uncertainties: Credit for predecessors
Whether the committee sees the contribution as a tool rather than a discovery
Competition from other econometrics entries

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theory of decision-making under ambiguity formalised the Ellsberg paradox and has been applied in finance, macro and robustness analysis. It is a significant conceptual contribution to decision theory.
assessment.attribution: Gilboa-Schmeidler (maxmin) and Schmeidler (Choquet) are the foundations. Schmeidler's death means he is not available, and the credited names are Gilboa, Epstein and Marinacci. Epstein is credited for recursive ambiguity-aversion applications in finance, and Marinacci for the later theory.
assessment.maturity: Foundational work from the late 1980s is mature. Empirical and applied validation is weaker than for other candidates.
uncertainties: Schmeidler's omission as a founder
Limited empirical or policy validation relative to higher-ranked entries
Whether the committee values pure decision theory at this point
